$comment: SCA rule catalog - rule sets. 'coverage' is the TARGET coverage we can reach with the listed backends. 'implemented' says whether SCA already runs it. Descriptions are our own words; official rule texts are copyrighted and not included.

coverageLevels.full: All checkable rules of the set can be covered.
coverageLevels.partial: A useful subset can be covered; the rest is missing or approximated.
coverageLevels.planned: Not covered by existing tools; needs our own checks (later phase).
coverageLevels.not-covered: Out of scope for now - see 'reason'.

backends.sca-native: Our own checks inside SCA (TypeScript or native engine).
backends.clang-analyzer: Clang Static Analyzer, path-sensitive bug finding (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception).
backends.cppcheck: Cppcheck core checks (GPL-3.0, run as a separate process only).
backends.cppcheck-misra: Cppcheck MISRA C addon (GPL-3.0, separate process; users supply rule texts from their own MISRA copy).
backends.frama-c-eva: Frama-C with the Eva abstract-interpretation plugin, C only (LGPL-2.1, separate process). Optional.

ruleSets.name: MISRA C:2012 (with amendments)
ruleSets.reason: Most decidable rules are checked by the Cppcheck MISRA addon. Some directives are about process/documentation (not tool-checkable), and 'undecidable' rules can only be approximated.

ruleSets.name: MISRA C:2023
ruleSets.reason: Large overlap with MISRA C:2012 (it consolidates the amendments). New guidelines need our own checks.

ruleSets.name: MISRA C++:2023
ruleSets.reason: No free tool covers it; Cppcheck support exists only in the paid Premium edition. Some rules overlap clang-tidy checks; the rest must be written by us on top of the Clang AST.

ruleSets.name: AUTOSAR C++14
ruleSets.reason: Partly overlaps clang-tidy (cppcoreguidelines-*, hicpp-*, bugprone-*). Largely superseded by MISRA C++:2023, so we map overlap first and add own checks by priority.

ruleSets.name: SEI CERT C
ruleSets.reason: clang-tidy has cert-* checks and the Clang Static Analyzer covers many run-time rules. Rules needing whole-program or concurrency analysis are missing.

ruleSets.name: SEI CERT C++
ruleSets.reason: Same as CERT C: good subset via clang-tidy cert-* and the analyzer, gaps in concurrency and whole-program rules.

ruleSets.name: CWE (mapping)
ruleSets.reason: CWE is a weakness list, not a rule set. We tag findings with CWE IDs where a backend check maps to one.

ruleSets.name: ISO/IEC TS 17961 (C secure coding)
ruleSets.reason: Strong overlap with CERT C; covered through the same checks.

ruleSets.name: HIS code metrics (complexity limits)
ruleSets.reason: Metrics (cyclomatic complexity, nesting, function size, parameters, ...) are straightforward to compute from the AST. Fully achievable by us.

ruleSets.name: Run-time errors - bug finding
ruleSets.reason: Division by zero, null dereference, uninitialized reads, out-of-bounds, leaks: found on many paths, but not proven absent (unsound by design).

ruleSets.name: Run-time errors - proof of absence (abstract interpretation)
ruleSets.reason: Sound proof needs a full abstract-interpretation engine (years of work). Frama-C Eva can be added later as an optional backend, but it supports C only - there is no mature open-source equivalent for C++.

ruleSets.name: Concurrency (data races, deadlocks)
ruleSets.reason: Needs a whole-program model of tasks/interrupts and shared data (OS/RTOS-specific). Free tools are weak here. Later phase.

ruleSets.name: JSF AV C++
ruleSets.reason: Aerospace legacy standard, not needed for automotive. Superseded by MISRA C++:2023.

ruleSets.name: SCA own rules
ruleSets.reason: Our own rules (naming, style, project conventions). No licensing limits.
